title: Angela, Stop!
mood: Ruby lands in a burning city and finds Angela fighting for Oro. She will not let her go.

hero.alt: Angela stands between two androids in a smoking city, her eyes glowing magenta.

segs.t: The ship came down in the middle of a burning avenue. The ramp fell open on smoke.
Ruby took her scythe from the rack by the hatch. It was white and orange, taller than she was. Her father had made sure the heir could fight.
A soldier barred the ramp. “Stay aboard, Heir. We will bring the weapon to you.”
Ruby looked past him. Androids with magenta eyes were walking through the smoke. Students in S·L·K jackets ran from them.

media.alt: A ship hovers low over a ruined street between broken towers, smoke rolling around it.

segs.t: “No... I’m not anyone’s puppet.”
She ducked under his arm and jumped.
Two students lay in the street, a boy and a girl, with a cracked training blade between them. An android’s fist was coming down on them. Ruby’s scythe met it at the wrist.

media.alt: Ruby throws out a hand in front of two students on the ground, her weapon over her shoulder.

segs.t: “Go!” The students ran.
She cut down the android, and the next, and the next. None of them spoke. When she stopped, one was left standing in the avenue.
She was small, with pink hair and white armor. A doll was pressed to her chest. Her eyes glowed red.
“Angela, stop!”
Angela walked at her, cold and blank, and swung. Ruby caught the blow on the scythe’s haft.
“I’m Ruby! Don’t you remember?” Nothing moved in Angela’s face. “We had been together since the very beginning!”

blocks.caption: I’m Ruby! Don’t you remember? We had been together since the very beginning!

media.alt: Ruby calls out on a broken bridge against a burning evening sky.

segs.t: Ruby threw out her free hand. “Code Override!” It rewrote a machine’s orders. Green lines ran from her glove and landed on Angela’s back, on the plate between her shoulder blades. Its small light burned red now. It had been dark on Oro.
The lines reached the Council’s seal and stopped. DENIED, said the air in red.

That was what the plate was. A control unit. It took the Council’s orders every second, and while it drove Angela’s body, its orders outranked anything Ruby wrote. Her code could not reach it from here. Her hands could.
She hooked the scythe across her back and stepped in.

Angela’s fist took her in the ribs. Every blow came a beat late. Ruby could have dodged them all, and she stopped dodging. The next one cracked her shoulder armor, and she stepped in again. Angela was far stronger than any human.
“I don’t want you to be like this!” Another blow. “I don’t want freedom at the cost of you!”

blocks.caption: I don’t want you to be like this! I don’t want freedom at the cost of you!

segs.t: Blood ran into her mouth. “Wake up, Angela!” she said. Then, lower: “How did we end up like this...”

media.alt: Close on Ruby shouting, with the ruined city behind her.

segs.t: She was inside the swing. She threw both arms around Angela and held on.
“I’m never letting go of you!”
Her fingers found the plate’s edge. In the lab, its light had stayed dark while Angela came back from a shutdown. Ruby clung to that. It did not say what happened when the plate was gone.
She tore it out.
Sparks burst from Angela’s back. The red went out of her eyes, and they turned gray. For three seconds she was herself.

media.alt: Ruby's hand pulls a glowing chip from Angela's back; close on Angela's eye as it fades from magenta to gray.

segs.t: “I think I know what hurt means now.”

blocks.caption: I think I know what hurt means now.

segs.t: Ruby could not breathe.
“I’m... hurting...” Angela’s hand lifted, and found nothing. “How do I stop it?”

blocks.caption: I’m... hurting... How do I stop it?

segs.t: Then her eyes closed. She went limp in Ruby’s arms. In Ruby’s fist, the plate’s light was out.

media.alt: Ruby holds Angela close, tears on her cheek, then opens her eyes.

segs.t: Ruby held her. She counted to ten, and to thirty. Angela did not move. Nobody had ever let Ruby open the plate. She did not know if a girl could live without it.
I said they would need me to shut her down,
she thought.
I did it. I killed her.
“If it wasn’t for all of this...”

blocks.caption: If it wasn’t for all of this...

segs.t: She laid Angela on the stones. She dropped the plate and brought her boot down on it, again and again, until the seal was gone. Grief turned into rage, and the rage did not care what it hit.
The rest of the company came down the avenue in rows. Ruby went to meet them. She cut down every one, and the lamp post behind them, and the wall.

media.alt: Seen from behind, Ruby stands with her scythe as androids leap at her through the flames.

segs.t: “If it wasn’t for all of this...”

blocks.caption: If it wasn’t for all of this...

segs.t: At the avenue’s end was a barrel. In front of it, holding a cracked training blade in both hands, stood the boy she had sent running. He had come back.
“Please,” he said. “It’s only a kid.”
She shoved him aside with one hand. The lid rocked. Inside, a small child sat with both hands over its ears, crying.

media.alt: Ruby knocks a student aside with her weapon; behind him a small child crouches in the rubble.

segs.t: Ruby raised the scythe. It climbed over her head and reached the top of its swing.
